findings.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — Eager initialization runs on an internally created background context that no caller can cancel until construction returns, so a hung backend or index build can block process startup and shutdown indefinitely.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:261 — Returning nil after Init partially succeeds performs no cancellation or rollback, so a later watcher failure leaks initialized lifecycle resources and the search watcher/open indexes and can make a retry fail on persistent-index locks.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:451 — Removing the Init guard from RPC methods also removes their stopped-state check, so requests arriving after Stop can continue reading or mutating an already-stopped backend.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216 — The new TotalDocs call ranges over the Bleve cache without its mutex after the event watcher starts, so a lazy index insertion can trigger a fatal concurrent-map iteration/write panic during startup.

pkg/server/module_server_test.go:36 — Unconditionally skipping this integration test for PostgreSQL turns its CI failure into a pass, leaving the eager storage-server startup path unverified on that backend.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — NewResourceServer now performs database and full-index I/O with an internally created background context, so callers cannot apply a startup deadline or cancel a hung construction.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:261 — Returning nil after eager initialization fails does not call Lifecycle.Stop or cancel, so failures after Lifecycle.Init succeeds leak partially initialized resources and make safe caller cleanup impossible.

pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — Restricting cacheMu to the final assignment lets concurrent misses build the same key simultaneously and the last completion can overwrite an index that already received newer watch events, leaving search results permanently stale.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216 — Calling TotalDocs after starting the event consumer can iterate Bleve's cache map concurrently with insertion of an index for a new resource, causing a concurrent-map panic because TotalDocs takes no read lock.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — Returning nil when eager Init fails abandons the server context and any lifecycle or search watcher started before a later initialization error, leaking active pollers and index resources and potentially preventing a clean retry.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:452 — Removing the Init guard from request handlers bypasses the stopped-state error stored by Stop, so reads and writes can continue against a server whose lifecycle and watchers have already been shut down.

pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:98 — Releasing the cache lock before construction lets concurrent misses for one key each build the full index, multiplying unbounded database scans and peak memory or disk use enough to exhaust the process.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — Eager initialization performs database setup and full indexing with a never-expiring internal context, so an unavailable backend or stalled scan can hang process startup forever.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:310 — Starting the search watcher before initWatcher means a subsequent initWatcher error leaves search.init's context.Background goroutine running after NewResourceServer returns nil, leaking a watcher on every retry.

pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — Locking only the cache assignment lets concurrent misses build the same key simultaneously, causing file-backed builds to fail or a later cache overwrite to discard events applied to the first index.

pkg/server/module_server_test.go:36 — Skipping the failing PostgreSQL case removes CI coverage for the storage-server startup path changed here, so a supported backend can remain unable to start undetected.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216 — No startup concurrency test covers an event-triggered Bleve cache insertion racing the new TotalDocs call, which can cause a fatal concurrent map iteration/write.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:303 — No integration test writes between the search and broadcaster subscriptions after this reorder, so SQL WatchWriteEvents can snapshot past the write and permanently omit it from client watch streams.

goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — Eager initialization runs on an internally created background context that no caller can cancel until construction returns, so a hung backend or index build can block process startup and shutdown indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that Init() is now called eagerly during NewResourceServer() at line 258. Looking at the context, NewResourceServer receives 'ctx' from ResourceServerOptions.Ctx (line 130 shows 'ctx := opts.Ctx'). The Init() method calls s.search.init(ctx) which can take significant time (the diff shows it logs 'duration_secs' and has index building). If the context passed to NewResourceServer is a background context that cannot be cancelled, and the backend or index build hangs, this would indeed block startup indefinitely. The finding correctly identifies that moving initialization from lazy (per-request) to eager (at construction) creates a potential blocking issue during startup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:261 — Returning nil after Init partially succeeds performs no cancellation or rollback, so a later watcher failure leaks initialized lifecycle resources and the search watcher/open indexes and can make a retry fail on persistent-index locks.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows Init() is now called during NewResourceServer() at line 255-260. Looking at the Init() method (lines 300-316), it performs multiple initialization steps in sequence: first search.init(ctx), then initWatcher(). If search.init() succeeds but initWatcher() fails, the code returns an error but doesn't clean up the already-initialized search index. The finding correctly identifies that partial initialization without rollback could leak resources. The diff removes lazy initialization from individual methods and moves it to constructor, making this a real concern for the new code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:451 — Removing the Init guard from RPC methods also removes their stopped-state check, so requests arriving after Stop can continue reading or mutating an already-stopped backend.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that Init() calls are being removed from multiple RPC methods (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob, GetBlob). Looking at the Init() method implementation (lines 294-320), it contains a sync.Once pattern that sets initErr and performs initialization checks. By removing these Init() guards from RPC methods, there's no longer a check for whether the server has been properly initialized or is in a stopped state before processing requests. The finding correctly identifies that requests could arrive after Stop() is called and still be processed against a stopped backend, since the Init() call that would have caught this state is now removed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/server/module_server_test.go:36 — Unconditionally skipping this integration test for PostgreSQL turns its CI failure into a pass, leaving the eager storage-server startup path unverified on that backend.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new skip condition being added for PostgreSQL tests with a TODO comment indicating it needs to be fixed. This is a legitimate concern - the test is being skipped rather than fixed, which means the new initialization changes in server.go (moving Init() to be called during NewResourceServer() and reordering search init before watcher init) won't be tested against PostgreSQL in CI. The finding correctly identifies that this reduces test coverage for an important code path change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — NewResourceServer now performs database and full-index I/O with an internally created background context, so callers cannot apply a startup deadline or cancel a hung construction.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, NewResourceServer creates a context with `ctx := context.Background()` at line 213 (not shown but referenced in the existing code structure), and the new code at lines 255-260 calls `s.Init(ctx)` with this internal context. The Init method performs database operations and search index initialization (as seen in the init method changes). Since the context is created internally with `context.Background()`, callers cannot pass their own context with deadlines or cancellation. This is a real defect - if initialization hangs, there's no way for the caller to timeout or cancel the operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:261 — Returning nil after eager initialization fails does not call Lifecycle.Stop or cancel, so failures after Lifecycle.Init succeeds leak partially initialized resources and make safe caller cleanup impossible.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that Init() is now called eagerly in NewResourceServer() at line 255-260. Looking at the Init() function (lines 300+), it calls s.lifecycle.Init(ctx) and other initialization steps. If s.Init(ctx) fails after s.lifecycle.Init() succeeds (e.g., during s.search.init() or s.initWatcher()), the function returns nil, err without calling s.lifecycle.Stop() or any cleanup. This would leak the partially initialized lifecycle resources. The finding correctly identifies that the new eager initialization pattern doesn't handle partial initialization cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216 — Calling TotalDocs after starting the event consumer can iterate Bleve's cache map concurrently with insertion of an index for a new resource, causing a concurrent-map panic because TotalDocs takes no read lock.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims TotalDocs() is called after starting the event consumer, but looking at the diff, line 216 shows the log statement with TotalDocs() is called BEFORE the watcher is initialized. The diff shows the order was changed: search.init(ctx) is now called BEFORE initWatcher(). The TotalDocs() call at line 216 happens within the init() function, before the goroutine in line 213 starts consuming events. Additionally, the finding claims TotalDocs iterates the cache map without a lock, but this is not verifiable from the diff - we cannot see the TotalDocs implementation. The concern about concurrent map access is speculative and not grounded in the actual code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — Returning nil when eager Init fails abandons the server context and any lifecycle or search watcher started before a later initialization error, leaking active pollers and index resources and potentially preventing a clean retry.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, when Init() is called at line 255-260 in NewResourceServer, if it fails, the function returns nil and the error. At this point, no 'server context', 'lifecycle', 'search watcher', or 'active pollers' have been started yet - those are all initialized INSIDE the Init() method itself. The Init() method uses sync.Once to ensure initialization happens only once, and if there's an error during initialization, it's stored in s.initErr. The finding claims resources are leaked before the error, but examining the Init() method shows that if an error occurs at any step, subsequent steps are skipped (due to the 'if s.initErr == nil' checks). There's no evidence of leaked resources when returning nil on Init failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:452 — Removing the Init guard from request handlers bypasses the stopped-state error stored by Stop, so reads and writes can continue against a server whose lifecycle and watchers have already been shut down.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that Init() calls are being removed from multiple request handlers (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob, GetBlob). The Init() method contains logic that checks s.initErr and returns it if set. Looking at the server struct, there's likely a Stop() method that sets an error state. By removing these Init() guards, the handlers no longer check if the server has been stopped or encountered initialization errors, potentially allowing operations to proceed on a stopped/errored server. The finding correctly identifies that removing these guards bypasses stopped-state error checking.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:98 — Releasing the cache lock before construction lets concurrent misses for one key each build the full index, multiplying unbounded database scans and peak memory or disk use enough to exhaust the process.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the lock acquisition (b.cacheMu.Lock()) was moved from before the index building logic (line 88-89 in old code) to after the index is built (line 137-139 in new code). This means the cache lookup and index building now happen without holding the lock, only acquiring it briefly to store the result. If multiple goroutines concurrently call BuildIndex for the same key, they will all see a cache miss and each proceed to build the full index independently, causing duplicate expensive database scans and memory/disk usage. This is a real race condition bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 — Eager initialization performs database setup and full indexing with a never-expiring internal context, so an unavailable backend or stalled scan can hang process startup forever.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that Init() is now called eagerly during NewResourceServer() at line 255-259. Looking at the Init() method, it calls s.search.init(ctx) which performs index initialization. The context passed to NewResourceServer comes from the caller, but the Init() method uses sync.Once and the context passed to it. If the backend is unavailable or indexing takes too long, this could indeed block startup. The finding correctly identifies that eager initialization with potentially long-running operations (database setup, full indexing) could hang the process. However, the claim about 'never-expiring internal context' is not fully verifiable from the diff - we can see ctx is passed through but cannot confirm it has no timeout.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:310 — Starting the search watcher before initWatcher means a subsequent initWatcher error leaves search.init's context.Background goroutine running after NewResourceServer returns nil, leaking a watcher on every retry.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in server.go Init(), the order was changed so search.init(ctx) is called before initWatcher(). Looking at search.go, the init() method starts a goroutine at line 213 ('go func() {...}()'). If search.init() succeeds but initWatcher() fails afterward, the server returns an error from NewResourceServer (lines 255-260), but the goroutine started by search.init() would continue running. This is a resource leak - the search watcher goroutine runs without proper cleanup when initialization fails partway through.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137 — Locking only the cache assignment lets concurrent misses build the same key simultaneously, causing file-backed builds to fail or a later cache overwrite to discard events applied to the first index.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the lock was moved from protecting the entire BuildIndex operation (lines 88-89 removed) to only protecting the cache assignment (lines 137-139 added). This means multiple concurrent calls for the same key can now execute the index building logic simultaneously. For file-backed indexes, this could cause conflicts when multiple goroutines try to create the same directory/files. Additionally, if two goroutines build indexes for the same key, the second one to acquire the lock will overwrite the first in the cache, potentially discarding any events that were applied to the first index between its creation and the overwrite.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/server/module_server_test.go:36 — Skipping the failing PostgreSQL case removes CI coverage for the storage-server startup path changed here, so a supported backend can remain unable to start undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a test being skipped for PostgreSQL with a TODO comment indicating it's a known issue that works locally but not in Drone CI. The finding correctly identifies that this reduces CI coverage for the storage-server startup path. However, this is not a bug introduced by the diff - it's a pragmatic decision to skip a flaky test with a TODO to fix it later. The concern about reduced coverage is valid and specific to the diff, making it an important non-bug issue rather than a hallucination, but it's also not a defect since the test is explicitly marked for future fixing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216 — No startup concurrency test covers an event-triggered Bleve cache insertion racing the new TotalDocs call, which can cause a fatal concurrent map iteration/write.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's a race condition between event-triggered Bleve cache insertion and TotalDocs call at line 216. Looking at the diff, line 216 shows a log statement `s.log.Info("search index initialized", "duration_secs", end-start, "total_docs", s.search.TotalDocs())`. The diff in bleve.go shows that the cache mutex lock was moved from the beginning of BuildIndex to just around the cache insertion (lines 137-139). However, TotalDocs() is called during init(), and the diff shows that initWatcher() (which would trigger events) is now called AFTER search.init() completes (lines 300-310 in server.go). This means events won't be processed until after TotalDocs is called during initialization. The finding misreads the execution order - the watcher that would trigger events is started after init completes, so there's no race at startup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:303 — No integration test writes between the search and broadcaster subscriptions after this reorder, so SQL WatchWriteEvents can snapshot past the write and permanently omit it from client watch streams.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's a race condition between search initialization and watcher initialization after the reorder. Looking at the diff, the change moves search.init(ctx) to happen BEFORE initWatcher(). The finding suggests this creates a problem where 'SQL WatchWriteEvents can snapshot past the write', but this is backwards - the new order actually ensures the search index is initialized before the watcher starts, which is a safer ordering. The finding misreads the implications of the reorder. Additionally, the diff shows Init() is now called during NewResourceServer() construction (lines 255-260), ensuring initialization happens once at startup rather than lazily on each request. The finding's claim about 'permanently omit it from client watch streams' is not substantiated by the diff.
